pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\nvoid initMatrix(std::vector<double>& mat, const size_t N) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[i * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, i, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid matrixMultiply(const std::vector<double>& A, const std::vector<double>& B, \n                    std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                sum += A[i * N + k] * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n            C[i * N + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a single element and compare\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& A, for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n            \n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += A[i * N + k] * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n            \n            const double actual = C[i * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n            \n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actual, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            N = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", N, N);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrices\n    std::vector<double> A(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> B(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> C(N * N);\n    \n    // Initialize matrices\n    printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    initMatrix(A, N);\n    initMatrix(B, N);\n    \n    // Perform matrix multiplication\n    printf(\"Computing matrix multiplication...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    matrixMultiply(A, B, C, N);\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate GFLOPS\n    double gflops = (2.0 * N * N * N) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(C, \"MatrixC\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateResult(A, B, C, N);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", N, N);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // std::vector<double> C_local(block.count * N);\n\n    // Initialize matrices\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    }\n    initRows(A, N, block.begin, block.count);\n    initRows(B, N, 0, N);\n\n    // Gather layout for assembling the full C on the root\n    std::vector<int> counts(size);\n    std::vector<int> displs(size);\n    for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfyMnRhU74ZEGkQuxMzFM","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The matmul benchmark now runs distributed across MPI ranks, unconditionally. Only `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt` changed, and the executable is still `matmul`.\n\n**Results**\n- **Correctness:** For N = 1, 3, 7, 100 and 513 at 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 16 ranks, the `-r` output (sums, min/max, samples, hash) matches the serial reference exactly. `-v` passes, and `-h` and unknown-option paths behave as before.\n- **Performance (N = 2048, same machine):** The original build took 99 s (0.17 GFLOPS). The MPI build takes 2.5 s on 1 rank and 180 ms on 16 ranks (95 GFLOPS), about 14× speedup from 1 to 16 ranks.\n\n**Design**\n- Rank `r` owns a contiguous block of C's rows. Every rank generates its rows of A and all of B locally, so no input broadcast is needed.\n- Each rank computes its rows with a cache-tiled i-k-j loop. For each C element, k still accumulates in increasing order, so the arithmetic matches the original.\n- `MPI_Gatherv` assembles the full C on rank 0, which prints the results and runs validation. Rank 0 regenerates the full A only when `-v` is set. The timed region covers the multiply and the gather.\n- Exit codes are broadcast from rank 0, so all ranks return the same status.\n- CMake now calls `find_package(MPI REQUIRED)` and links `MPI::MPI_CXX`.\n\n**Decisions for you to check**\n- **`-ffp-contract=off` added to the compile flags.** Without it, GCC fused multiply-adds differently in the tiled and vectorized code, so results depended on tiling. This flag makes results identical for any rank count.\n- **Output differs from the original's default build in the last bits for some N.** The original's default build (which fuses multiply-adds) produces different hashes for N = 7 and N = 513, although it matches for N = 100. I couldn't find an explicit-FMA formulation that matches the default build bit-for-bit. Results match the original compiled with `-ffp-contract=off`, which is the configuration I verified.\n- **Timing output.** The timing line is now computed from MPI_Wtime, and the GFLOPS figure uses the unrounded seconds. The original derived GFLOPS from integer milliseconds. The printed format is unchanged.\n- **Extra dependency and portability notes.** The build needs an MPI installation (OpenMPI is present here). The build was verified with OpenMPI 3.1, GCC 13 and CMake, and built in `/tmp` so the repo has no build artifacts."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":949,"cache_read_input_tokens":49401,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":949},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cfa2abc8-31d2-442a-8ec9-39563ea77a58","uuid":"99c50c04-5326-49cd-a10f-32ecb718e8c7","timestamp":"2026-10-13T01:21:18.969Z","request_id":"req_011CfyMnRRMBCnocoWZ5hi39"}
